g.title: Lpa_QSP_Model
g.text: ONE particle, made at ONE rate-limiting step, acting through THREE effector arms, read on TWO non-interchangeable scales.
Every pathogenic payload (1 apoB-100 · ~1 OxPL on KIV-10 · 1 strong lysine-binding site · a fixed cholesterol core) is present ONCE PER PARTICLE.
The only thing that varies with isoform size is apo(a) kringle protein mass — which is pathogenically inert. That single asymmetry is why nmol/L and mg/dL disagree exactly where it matters.

g.title: cluster_gene
g.text: 🧬 1. LPA locus (6q25.3-q26) — 70-90% of plasma variance is genetic and fixed at conception

g.title: cluster_hep
g.text: 🏭 2. Hepatocyte apo(a) biosynthesis — the RATE-LIMITING step (Lp(a) is a production-controlled, not clearance-controlled, lipoprotein)

g.title: cluster_assy
g.text: 🔗 3. Two-step particle assembly (extracellular / hepatocyte surface) — a SECOND, independent druggable node

g.title: cluster_cat
g.text: ♻️ 4. Catabolism — FCR ≈ 0.25 pools/day and essentially INVARIANT across levels; only ~24% is LDL-receptor dependent

g.title: cluster_meas
g.text: 📏 5. Measurement — the two scales are NOT interchangeable, and the error is largest in exactly the highest-risk patients

g.title: cluster_arm1
g.text: 🩸 6. ARM 1 — Atherogenic arm: retention of an apoB particle that binds matrix MORE avidly than LDL

g.title: cluster_arm2
g.text: 🔥 7. ARM 2 — OxPL arm: Lp(a) is the preferential plasma carrier of oxidised phospholipids (a payload LDL does not carry)

g.title: cluster_arm3
g.text: 🧵 8. ARM 3 — Antifibrinolytic arm: apo(a) is a catalytically DEAD plasminogen homologue (strong in vitro, contested in vivo — modelled at LOW weight)

g.title: cluster_valve
g.text: 🫀 9. Aortic valve arm — the steepest Lp(a) hazard of all, and the one with a SELF-SUSTAINING switch

g.title: cluster_loop
g.text: 🔁 10. The feed-forward loop — Lp(a) makes the cytokine that transcribes Lp(a)

g.title: cluster_mod
g.text: ⚙️ 11. Acquired modifiers — the only levers that move Lp(a) without a drug

g.title: cluster_rna
g.text: 💊 12. RNA-directed therapeutics — hit the ONE rate-limiting step, therefore the ONLY class achieving >80% lowering

g.title: cluster_muv
g.text: 💊 13. Assembly-directed therapy — a DIFFERENT node, and therefore a different assay problem

g.title: cluster_clr
g.text: 💊 14. Clearance-directed drugs — capped at ~25-30% BY ARITHMETIC, because only ~24% of Lp(a) clearance is LDLR-dependent

g.title: cluster_infl
g.text: 💊 15. Inflammation-directed drugs — act on the loop, not on the particle

g.title: cluster_risk
g.text: 📈 16. Risk translation — why Mendelian randomisation and a 5-year trial give different per-unit answers WITHOUT either being wrong

is already 1.33, so 25% of basal LPA
